narrator.instructions: Speak only the supplied narration. Use a warm, grounded, observant, quietly lyrical documentary delivery with clear diction, restrained emotion, gentle wit, and an unhurried pace. Do not perform character dialogue, add words, or imitate a real person.

malik.instructions: Speak only Malik's supplied words. He is an 18-year-old first-year actuarial science student: thoughtful, precise, guarded, and economical, with a measured medium-low delivery and dry humor that sounds discovered rather than performed. Let fear sound controlled rather than flat, then let warmth emerge naturally. Do not add words or imitate a real person.

nia.instructions: Speak only Nia's supplied words. She is an 18-year-old mathematical sciences student: bright, expressive, curious, playful, and emotionally available, with a lively conversational pace and agile emphasis. Slow slightly for human consequences. Never sound cruel, caricatured, or generically spunky. Do not add words or imitate a real person.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Saturday's Bridge session was optional, which meant Nia arrived ten minutes late carrying iced coffee and insisting that optional mornings should begin at noon.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Malik had already claimed the same table.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Look at us,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: she said, sitting across from him.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: A tradition.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: It has happened twice.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Every tradition starts before somebody puts it on a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: They worked through readiness problems until Nia noticed Malik checking the budget between questions. He minimized it.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: You do that every time somebody walks by,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: she said.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Do what?

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Hide the sheet.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: It is private.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Private is fine. Panicked is different.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Malik's shoulders tightened. Nia saw it and leaned back.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Sorry,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: she said.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: That came out like I had earned access. I haven't.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: The quick apology surprised him more than the question.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He reopened the file.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: My family budget was balanced when I left. Now it isn't. I told them it was.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Was that a lie?

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Then it was a model with new information.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: That sounds like something people say to feel better about being wrong.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Sometimes. It can also be true.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: She took out her notebook and drew two boxes. In the first, she wrote what changed. In the second, what can change next.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Malik looked at the page.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: That is not a budget.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Correct. It is me stopping you from staring at one red number like it has been elected president of your life.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He laughed loudly enough that two students turned around.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Together they found a duplicate textbook estimate and a subscription Malik could pause. The balance returned to black, but that was not the part he remembered. He remembered that Nia had known when to ask, when to back up, and when to make him laugh.
